LEARN / SEE BOTH SIDES

Understand what you’re buying into.

Read the buyer side and the supply side. Test why demand might arrive—and who controls the inventory, permissions, liquidity, and incentives behind the token.

Supply hygiene helps uncover structural risks. It does not guarantee market demand. A convincing story does not clear the supply checks.

What every lesson should help you do

Understand what it is, how it works, where and how to check, what the evidence means, and what you still cannot see.

Your learning path

  1. 101A · Understand the basics
  2. 101B · Check thesis and hygiene
  3. 101C · Understand the dev and supply
  4. Choose your market lens: 202A · Snipe or 202B · Swing
  5. 303A · Manage your exposure

Start with 101A if you are new. Use 101B and 101C before applying a market lens; Snipe and Swing are alternatives for different questions. Return to earlier checks when conditions change.

START HERE / 101A

Foundations

What am I looking at?

Token numbers, launch, ownership, flow, attention, and risk.8 foundation levels →THEN / 101B

Survival & Hygiene

Should I touch it?

Separate the upside story from what could destroy the trade. Check the token, the demand, and your own decisions.8 chapters with worked investigations →THEN / 101C

Understand the Dev & Supply

What am I buying into—and what can the supply side do?

See beyond the visible dev wallet. Understand who controls supply, what they can change or sell, how they earn, and how their incentives affect buyers.13 chapters with worked investigations →CHOOSE YOUR LENS / 202A

Snipe

Why is it accelerating now?

Read changes in demand before the move becomes obvious: buyers, size, selling, absorption, and attention.11 chapters with worked investigations →CHOOSE YOUR LENS / 202B

Swing

Has it earned another tradable cycle?

Read the structure after the first move, then check fresh demand, persistent attention, and the changing market environment.11 chapters with worked investigations →MANAGE YOUR EXPOSURE / 303A

Managing Your Position

How much capital and time does it deserve, and how do I leave?

Set exposure limits, require evidence before adding, harvest deliberately, and reassess the next decision.11 chapters with worked investigations →

Build the case, then check it

101A explains the token. 101B separates the demand thesis from hygiene. 101C teaches the creator and supply mechanics, then the dev–buyer relationship. Together they prepare you to investigate the early move in 202A or later structure in 202B. 303A turns that evidence into exposure limits, reassessment, and exit planning.
